title: FP8 instability stepwise playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal playbook / breadcrumb trail for investigating intermittent quality regressions and NaNs that show up with FP8 kernels. This is my working log — half checklist, half scratchpad — aimed at making the next on-call or triage faster.

Context / recent incident summary:
- Model: Llama-variant (config-mod) used with our optimized runtime + FP8 path enabled via --quant-mode fp8-alpha.
- Symptom: Occasional token collapse + generation of ‘nan’ logits in step N (typically after long context, 512+).
- Frequency: ~3% of requests in nightly A/B test with deterministic seed=42, rare in BF16 run.
- Impact: Quality regression alerts, some degraded downstream reranking scores.

Observed behaviors:
- When FP8 path is enabled: loss spikes after ~400 tokens, KV-cache values occasionally NaN.
- Running same inputs under BF16/FP32: no NaNs, normal perplexity curve.
- INT8 fast path (experimental): some quantization noise but no NaNs.
- Repro runs show that exact seed + same batch order sometimes reproduces, sometimes not (non-determinism likely from async kernels / atomic ops).

Immediate triage checklist (what I actually ran):
1) Reproduce locally with identical docker image and CUDA version.
   - docker run --gpus all -it redwood/runtime:nightly-2024-03-18 /bin/bash
2) Deterministic single-threaded run to eliminate async scheduling differences:
   - export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
   - python reproduce_fp8.py --model ./models/llama-mod --quant fp8 --seed 42 --batch 1 --ctx 1024
3) Log KV cache stats and per-layer min/max/mean before/after each attention block (quick patch in runtime):
   - added runtime hooks: log_tensor_stats(layer_idx, kv.key, kv.value)
4) Binary search: disable half of layers to localize (binary-skip toggle):
   - for i in range(0, n_layers, 2): python reproduce_fp8.py --disable-layers "$i"
5) Cross-check weight ranges vs expected dynamic range: quant-calibration dump script:
   - python quant_dump.py --model weights.pt --out weight_ranges.csv

Key commands and snippets I used (copyable):
- reproduce command (single GPU, blocking):
  OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python reproduce_fp8.py --model models/llama-mod --quant fp8 --seed 42 --max-tokens 2048 --log-kv --save-trace trace_fp8_seed42.json

- quick kernel stress (loop many sequences to increase chance of hitting NaN):
  for i in $(seq 1 200); do python reproduce_fp8.py --seed $i --quant fp8 --max-tokens 1024 --silent; done | tee runloop.log

- diff BF16 vs FP8 traces (very rough):
  jq '.kv_stats | map(select(.has_nan==true))' trace_fp8_seed42.json > fp8_nans.json
  jq '.kv_stats | map(select(.has_nan==true))' trace_bf16_seed42.json > bf16_nans.json

Error / traceback excerpts captured:
- Runtime assertion in CUDA kernel (translated by debug build):
  Assertion failed: !isnan(scale) at quantize_fp8.cu:128
  GPU stack dump:
    at quantize_kernel (quantize_fp8.cu:128)
    at apply_attention (attention.cu:431)
    at forward_pass (runtime.cc:279)

- Python-level evidence (from trace):
  Layer 22: kv_key min = -nan, kv_value mean = nan, attention scores contain nan -> later softmax returns nan

Experimental results log (short table, CSV-like):
- run_id,quant,seed,ctx,nan_detected,first_nan_layer
- r1,fp8,42,1024,true,22
- r2,fp8,7,1024,true,22
- r3,bf16,42,1024,false,-1
- r4,int8,42,1024,false,-1

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) FP8 dynamic range clipping/scale underflow: a combination of outlier activations and an approximate scale update leads to divide-by-zero or subnormal values that the kernel mishandles.
2) Race condition in async fused kernels when writing KV cache: partial writes + mixed precision promotes to NaN under certain interleavings.
3) Quantization calibration mismatch: per-tensor vs per-channel scale choice causes overflow in some layers only.
4) Kernel numerical bug triggered by extreme sequence lengths (KV-rotation arithmetic edge case).

Evidence for/against hypotheses: 
- H1: weight/value ranges show some extremely small scales (~1e-38) on the failing layer in fp8 runs. Supports underflow idea.
- H2: Enabling CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 reduces repro frequency dramatically (was reproducible 3% -> <0.1%), suggests scheduling/race component.
- H3: Re-running with per-channel calibration reduced but did not eliminate failures.
- H4: Failures concentrate after long prefix (>=400 tokens), might involve rotation index math; still plausible.

Quick patches I tried and their outcome:
- Force clamp in quantize kernel: clamp(scale, 1e-8, 1e8) -> reduced NaNs but created minor accuracy drift (~0.4% hit in eval metric).
- Introduced atomic-safe write for KV cache in one layer -> removed NaNs for that specific layer in isolated test.
- Fallback: if nan observed in logits, re-run that request in BF16 as transient mitigation (adds latency but saves correctness).

Longer-term mitigations to propose:
- Robust scale stabilization: add tiny epsilon and smoothed EMA to any dynamic scale computed for FP8.
- Formalize a deterministic path for production repro tests (deterministic kernels for CI) to ensure race conditions are surfaced.
- Add per-layer guardrails in runtime: after quantize step, assert finite and fall back to higher precision per-layer if necessary.
- Better calibration tooling: per-channel auto-calibration with synthetic stimuli representing long sequence behavior.

Next steps (concrete):
- Patch A: add small epsilon to scale compute + add unit test that triggers underflow -> PR in runtime (linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/812). Target: low-risk, small perf cost.
- Patch B: add optional atomic-safe KV write compile flag to test perf vs reliability tradeoff (bench in nightly).
- Telemetry: add a lightweight NaN-rate metric (per model/quant-mode) to Console with alert threshold 0.1% per hour.
- Repro harness: build deterministic-quant-ci job with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and single-threaded to increase signal.

Notes to self / remember:
- When filing Jira, include both the trace JSON and the weight_range CSV (they were most informative).
- If we see same layer repeatedly, prioritize that layer for disabling FP8 in rollout policy.
- Talk to HW team about whether any driver-level known issues exist for certain GPU architectures (a100 vs h100 differences observed once).

Open questions / things to try next time:
- Try with flush-to-zero disabled/enabled at driver level (FTZ and denormals) to see effect on subnormals.
- Instrument warp-level divergence checks in the kernel (only in debug builds).
- Run stress profile using mixed sequences (random lengths) to see if specific token patterns trigger it.

Appendix: small checklist to hand to on-call
- If an FP8 NaN alert fires: 1) gather trace_fp8*.json from the job, 2) run single-run reproduce with blocking (see command above), 3) flip to BF16 fallback for that model in rollout, 4) ping eng-applied-ml on Slack with initial findings.

End of scratchpad.

(Will convert to Confluence postmortem if we identify a deterministic root cause.)
